It is 11.5 mi behind you if you're heading west, so it only makes sense for a rest day. Open lot with no designated tent pads. Animals and noise during events. No fires on pavement, no firearms.

bestBet: BLM dispersed: desert tracks between AZ 238 and Empire Blvd (south end of Sierra Estrella) — tents allowed

options.name: BLM dispersed: desert tracks between AZ 238 and Empire Blvd (south end of Sierra Estrella)
options.priceNote: Free; no permit. BLM limit is 14 days in any 28-day period.
options.locationNote: BLM public land along the route's dirt tracks north of AZ 238 near N Rahma St, Maricopa County — 10.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 46 from Casa Grande. On the line itself. From about mile 31.3 (N Rahma St off AZ 238) the route leaves pavement and follows unnamed OSM tracks across BLM land north to 'Empire Blvd'. Surface is dirt and sand with wash crossings; BLM calls these roads 'extremely sandy or silty' and requires 4WD to reach the wilderness boundary. Per BLM's land-status GIS, the line is on BLM land for most of miles 31-42.
options.booking: None; first come.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: Free, legal, no facilities at all. At miles 39-42 camp WEST of the north-south track: the Sierra Estrella Wilderness boundary is just east, and bikes are banned inside (the line passes about 165 ft from it at mile 42). A mapped BLM vault toilet sits at the Quartz Peak trailhead, about 1.7 mi east of mile 41.7, but the way there is deep sand. Tribal land is only 0.3-1 mi away near miles 28-34, so don't stray onto it. Carry all water from Maricopa; nothing is available from mile 25 to 58. Rainbow Valley BLM land gets target shooters, so camp out of sight of the track. Fireworks and exploding targets are banned year-round; seasonal fire restrictions were lifted July 22, 2026. No Lower Sonoran camping closures or BLM Arizona alerts were listed on Nov 1, 2026.

options.name: BLM dispersed: unpaved W Riggs Rd section (miles 45-47)

options.booking: None.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: The last free camp right on the line before pavement resumes. Rainbow Valley homes start just west; only the BLM block is legal, so stay clear of private parcels. No water; the nearest is a fire station about 12 mi ahead (mile 57.8).

options.booking: 7 primitive sites (A-G). Reserve online through the City of Buckeye at least 3 days ahead; unreserved walk-up stays are limited to one night (Dec 2025 review). Max 7 nights. The gate reportedly locks around 10 pm (one report says 9:30 pm), so arrive early.
options.cyclistIntel: Legal, cheap, quiet and dark, but completely dry: the city says there is no drinking water in the park. Fill up in Buckeye (Circle K on Monroe Ave) before the climb. Sites C-E are farther from the busy trailhead. It is a 17-mi round-trip detour north, not on the way west.

People were still camping there in Jan-Feb 2026, and a sheriff patrols mornings. Reviews from 2021-2026 report heavy shooting (ricochets near a trailer in Aug 2024), theft, dumping and crowding. Not a good place for a solo tent.

options.priceNote: $25/night 'Dry Camping', plus a $2.50 booking fee, a 3% card fee and tax ($125/week). Hookup sites are $35-50.

Confirm the dry site takes a tent when you book. Walking distance to everything in town.

options.priceNote: In season (Sept 15-Apr 15) the cheapest legal permit is the $40 short-visit permit covering any 14 consecutive days; there's no one-night rate. The long-term permit is $180. A 2024 BLM plan proposed $200/$600, but I found no sign it was adopted.
options.locationNote: US 95 south of I-10, Quartzsite, AZ 85346. Coordinates are the Tyson Wash host station, where permits are sold. — 3.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. About 2 miles south of Quartzsite on US 95 (from I-10 exit 17), with four sub-areas. Permits are sold at the entrance host station. Dirt roads inside, reported rough after the 2026 flooding.

options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: The only Quartzsite camp with public water taps (8, though a reviewer calls the water salty, so carry drinking water), 10 vault toilets, dump and trash. Poor value for one night next to the free 14-day areas.

options.name: Road Runner BLM 14-day camping area
options.priceNote: Free, 14-day limit. A host issues free permits in season.
options.locationNote: La Paz Valley Rd, Quartzsite, AZ 85346 — 6.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 184 from Casa Grande. About 6 miles south of I-10 on US 95 to milepost 99, then just west via N 53rd St / La Paz Valley Rd. Hard-packed gravel, with a steep drop-off at the road edge.
options.booking: First-come.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)

bestBet: McIntyre RV Resort (Peter McIntyre County Park) — tents, showers, water

options.name: Ehrenberg–Cibola Road BLM Dispersed Camping
options.priceNote: Free. Rangers enforce the 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, southeast of Ehrenberg, AZ 85334 — 3.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 201 from Casa Grande. From the Flying J at I-10 exit 1, take the south frontage road to Cibola Rd, which becomes Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd heading southeast. It is compacted gravel, washboarded for about 2 mi. Pull off onto open BLM desert about 3–3.5 mi from the exit.
options.booking: First come, any hour
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: The free fallback on the Arizona bank if the river parks are full or you arrive after the offices close. A Nov 2024 camper said you can barely hear I-10 from here. OHVs can raise dust at times. Fill water at the Flying J or Chevron at exit 1. BLM's Sandbowl page confirms dispersed camping is available in this area.

options.name: Villa Verde RV & Mobile Park
options.priceNote: Unknown. $21 was reported earlier and $40 cash in 2022.
options.locationNote: 50221 Ehrenberg-Poston Hwy, Ehrenberg, AZ 85334 — 0.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 203 from Casa Grande. Paved. I-10 exit 1, then 1/4 mi north on Poston Rd and 1/8 mi west.
options.booking: Pay cash at the office. A 2022 camper said the office staff disappeared.
options.cyclistIntel: A run-down mobile-home park with some RV sites. A 2021 review says there are no showers and no bathrooms. Use it only as a last resort.

options.name: Ehrenberg Sandbowl (BLM OHV area)
options.priceNote: Free
options.locationNote: Off Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd, south of I-10 exit 1, Ehrenberg, AZ — 1.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 203 from Casa Grande. BLM directions: from the Ehrenberg exit take the south frontage road about 1 mi west, then turn left onto gravel Ehrenberg/Cibola Rd. The bowl itself is very soft sand, and a 2021 visitor's vehicle got stuck. Expect to push the bike.
options.booking: None
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: Camping here is legal, but it's an OHV playground with dust and engine noise. Ehrenberg–Cibola Rd, 3.5 mi out, is the better free choice.

options.name: Arizona Oasis RV Resort
options.priceNote: No tent rate published. RV sites run $63–115.
options.locationNote: 50238 Ehrenberg-Poston Hwy, Ehrenberg, AZ 85334 — 0.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 203 from Casa Grande. Paved, at I-10 exit 1 on the Arizona riverbank.
options.booking: Book online (RMS) or call. Check-in 12 PM, check-out 11 AM. The park is gated.
options.cyclistIntel: An older listing description mentioned 'tent camping', but the 2026 website lists only RV sites, cabins and rentals. Call before counting on it. It has a pool, spa and river beach. The Flying J is next door.

options.name: Levee Road BLM Dispersed Camping (Colorado River, AZ side)
options.priceNote: Free, 14 days
options.locationNote: Levee Rd south of Ehrenberg, AZ (across the river from McIntyre Park) — 8.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 204 from Casa Grande. 8–9 mi south of Ehrenberg on a washboard dirt levee road. One 2018 driver took 1.5 hours to cover 11 mi in an RV. There are OHVs on weekends.
options.booking: None
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: Riverfront spots, but rough, trashy in places and a long dirt slog with a loaded bike (Dec 2025 review). Only worth it if you want the river. McIntyre's paid tent sites are directly across the water.

options.name: McIntyre RV Resort (Peter McIntyre County Park)
options.priceNote: Standard tent site from $38/night, beachfront tent site from $43 (Campspot, Nov 2026). A 30-amp RV site is $50 if you need power.
options.locationNote: 8750 Peter D McIntyre Ave, Blythe, CA 92225 — 7.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 204 from Casa Grande. All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go south on Intake Blvd under I-10 for about 6 mi, then turn left onto Peter D McIntyre Ave (asphalt). About 6.6 mi one way.
options.booking: Book on Campspot (campspot.com/park/mcintyre-rv-resort-blythe-ca); walk-ins welcome. Office 7am to 4pm daily, California time.
options.cyclistIntel: About 20 tent sites on grass by the river, with newly renovated hot showers and restrooms for registered guests, a small store (ice and snacks), free Wi-Fi and a lagoon. New owners since June 1, 2025. A Campspot review from Oct 2026 and a Campendium review from Nov 2025 confirm it's open. Tent sites have no outlet.

options.name: The Cove RV Resort (formerly Riviera RV Resort)
options.priceNote: Tent rate by phone. RV sites are $60/night plus Blythe's 10% lodging tax.
options.locationNote: 500 Riviera Dr, Blythe, CA 92225 — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 204 from Casa Grande. Paved. Just over the Colorado River on the California side, at Riviera Dr (I-10 exit 243). It is 0.1–0.5 mi from where the bike/foot bridge and I-10 land. One reviewer called the access road 'sketchy'.
options.booking: Call; the office is open 8am to 5pm daily, California time. The store is open 8–5 Sunday to Thursday and 8–6 Friday and Saturday. A 2020 guest got a site at 9:30 pm, but call ahead for a late arrival.
options.cyclistIntel: The operator's own listing on The Dyrt (verified 2023) says: 'Backpacking instead of traveling by RV? We have sites to accommodate every kind of traveler, whether by bike, trailer or RV.' Campendium also tags it for tents. The 2026 website lists only RV sites, park models and day use, so confirm the tent rate. Restrooms and showers were recently renovated, and there's coin laundry, a pool and spa, Wi-Fi (new in 2026) and a store. This is the closest paid tent option to the line on the whole segment.

options.name: Mayflower County Park (Riverside County)
options.priceNote: Tent or dry site about $35 (2023 dry-camp rate) and possibly higher now. Sites with water and electric were $49 in Sept 2026. Booking yourself online added an $8 fee in 2023.
options.locationNote: 4980 Colorado River Rd, Blythe, CA 92225 — 7.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 205 from Casa Grande. All paved. From Hobsonway at Intake Blvd, go north on Intake Blvd (US 95) about 3.3 mi, east on 6th Ave 2.5 mi, then follow Colorado River Rd 0.5 mi to its end in the park. About 6.7 mi one way.
options.booking: Riverside County reservations online (rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches) or call the office. Check-in is reported quick and friendly. Office hours not verified, so call before arriving late. Maximum stay 14 nights.
options.cyclistIntel: There is a separate tent and dry-camping area by the river (27 dry sites), plus 152 sites with water and electric for power. Hot showers and flush toilets, but only one bathhouse and it's far from some sites. Water spigots are everywhere, though one reviewer said the water tastes odd. Reviews from Sept and Oct 2026 confirm it's open and clean. There are no services nearby, so shop in Blythe first.

bestBet: BLM land at Wiley's Well Rd, I-10 exit 222 (beside Wiley's Well Rest Area) — tents allowed

options.name: BLM land at Wiley's Well Rd, I-10 exit 222 (beside Wiley's Well Rest Area)
options.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit. No LTVA permit is needed because this is outside the Mule Mountain LTVA. Water and flush toilets are at the rest area 0.3 mi away, 24 h.
options.locationNote: Wiley's Well Rd at I-10 exit 222 (north side), 15 mi west of Blythe — 0.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 226 from Casa Grande. Leave I-10 at exit 222. The Wiley's Well Rest Area sits on Wiley's Well Rd just north of the freeway. Ride a few hundred yards north on paved Wiley's Well Rd, or along the dirt powerline track parallel to I-10, and camp on open BLM desert out of sight of the road. Flat, firm ground.
options.booking: None. You may NOT sleep inside the rest area itself: Caltrans has an 8-hour limit and no tents.
options.legalityNote: Legality not confirmed: read the notes before you pitch
options.cyclistIntel: Not a documented campsite; legal by land status. The BLM surface-management map shows BLM on every side of the interchange, inside Chuckwalla National Monument, and OSM shows no solar fencing here. It is the only spot between Blythe and Chiriaco where a dry camp sits beside water and toilets. It is 10 mi past the last store (BB Travel Center, exit 232) and 50 mi before Chiriaco. Two state prisons are 3 mi south, so stay north of I-10. Check for 'closed to camping' signs. Caltrans plans a rest-area water rebuild with no dates announced.

options.name: Wiley's Well Campground (Mule Mountain LTVA, BLM)
options.priceNote: $40 LTVA short-visit permit, required Sept 15-Apr 15. It covers 14 consecutive days at any CA/AZ LTVA; there is no nightly rate.
options.locationNote: Wiley's Well Rd, 9 mi south of I-10 exit 222 — 9 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 226 from Casa Grande. Exit 222, then south on Wiley's Well Rd: 3 mi paved past the Chuckwalla Valley and Ironwood state prisons, then 6 mi of graded dirt that is normally washboarded. BLM notice dated Oct 15, 2026: the road was damaged by Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel, is 'impassable for RVs and trailers', and is 4x4 only. A loaded bike will be slow, with possible walking. 18 mi round trip.
options.booking: No reservations. Buy the permit from the camp host (not always present) or a BLM office. Tents are allowed only at designated sites within 500 ft of the vault toilet.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: A real campground with tables, fire rings, a very clean vault toilet, trash and a dump station, but NO water; bring it from the rest area 9 mi back. Coon Hollow, 3 mi further south on the same damaged road, takes the same permit. Probably not worth the detour this week.

bestBet: BLM land at Corn Springs Rd, I-10 exit 201 (south-west of the interchange) — tents allowed

options.name: BLM land at Corn Springs Rd, I-10 exit 201 (south-west of the interchange)
options.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: Corn Springs Rd / Chuckwalla Valley Rd at I-10 exit 201, 9 mi east of Desert Center — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 247 from Casa Grande. Exit 201, south side. Paved Chuckwalla Valley Rd meets Corn Springs Rd at the ramps; go a few hundred yards west of Corn Springs Rd onto BLM desert. Keep clear of the fenced Maverick Solar project north and east of the exit.
options.booking: None.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map, inside Chuckwalla National Monument). It saves the sandy 7.8-mi ride to Corn Springs campground. A dry camp: the nearest water is Wiley's Well RA, 21 mi back, or Chiriaco, 29 mi ahead. Small dirt service roads (pipeline/utility) criss-cross the area.

options.name: Corn Springs Campground (BLM)
options.priceNote: $6/night, first come first served, 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: Corn Springs Rd, Chuckwalla Mountains, Desert Center, CA 92239 — 7.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 251 from Casa Grande. Exit 201, then south and west on Corn Springs Rd: about 7-8 mi of compacted/graded dirt with soft sandy wash crossings (a 2019 review said '4WD recommended'), climbing gently to about 1,600 ft. Condition after the October 2026 storm is unknown.
options.booking: First come, first served: 9 sites including 1 group site, no reservations. Quiet hours 9pm-8am.
options.cyclistIntel: A palm oasis with petroglyphs, shade ramadas, tables and grills; usually nearly empty midweek. BLM lists potable water, but a Jan 30, 2026 visitor reported 'No water available', so carry all you need. The round trip is more than 15 mi of dirt and sand. The Countri Bike rider (2016-17) considered it and went on to Chiriaco.

options.name: BLM land south of Desert Center, I-10 exit 192
options.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: South side of I-10 exit 192, Desert Center, CA 92239 — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 257 from Casa Grande. Exit 192 (Desert Center). On the south side a rough dirt track (OSM grade 4) runs south-west across BLM land; camp a few hundred yards in. Off limits: the town lots, the Caltrans yard, and the fenced Oberon/Athos solar fields north and east of the exit.
options.booking: None.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map). Halfway between Blythe and Chiriaco. Desert Center has NO store, water or gas, so carry dinner, breakfast and water for the 19 mi to Chiriaco. Lake Tamarisk Library, 2 mi north, has a fountain only Tue/Thu/Sat in the daytime.

options.name: BLM land north of Eagle Mountain Rd, I-10 exit 189
options.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: Eagle Mountain Rd at I-10 exit 189, 3 mi west of Desert Center — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 260 from Casa Grande. Exit 189, then north on paved Eagle Mountain Rd. BLM desert lies on both sides just north of the interchange.
options.booking: None.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: Undocumented; legal by land status (BLM surface-management map; no solar fields mapped here). An alternative to the Desert Center exit. Dry camp.

bestBet: Red Cloud Mine Road Dispersed Camping (BLM) — tents allowed

options.name: Red Cloud Mine Road Dispersed Camping (BLM)
options.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: Red Cloud Mine Rd at I-10 exit 182, Desert Center, CA 92239 — 0.9 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 266 from Casa Grande. Exit 182 (Red Cloud Rd), south side. A big gravel lot sits right by I-10, and dispersed sites run along a 2.2-mi graded dirt road toward the Chuckwalla Mtns. Light washboard and dips, with soft sand in places: a 2WD van got stuck in 2022.
options.booking: None.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: The only DOCUMENTED dispersed area near the line between Blythe and Chiriaco (Campendium, 6 reviews, latest Apr 2023). Freeway noise near the lot, a high-voltage line nearby, Border Patrol around. It is 9.5 mi before the Chiriaco store, which makes it the stop if daylight runs out (sunset is about 4:45 pm PST). No water.

options.name: Chiriaco Summit - Patton Museum Dry Camp Area
options.priceNote: Free. There are no facilities at the sites; water and restrooms are at the Chevron food mart (open 24 h) and the coffee shop, 400 m away.
options.locationNote: Behind the General Patton Memorial Museum, 62450 Chiriaco Rd, Chiriaco Summit, CA 92201 — 0.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 276 from Casa Grande. Exit 173. Paved to the museum, then take the dirt access road on the right side of the museum (sign: 'Welcome to Chiriaco Summit Dry Camp Area') to marked sites behind it. About 0.3 mi; the Chevron and cafe are about 400 m away.
options.booking: First come, first served. A camp host takes your name and plate number. If you arrive after dark, set up and check in the next morning (Dec 2024 review). Maximum stay is 5-7 nights.
options.cyclistIntel: The key camp on this segment: free, hosted, on BLM land, with marked sites including tent-only spots and stone fire rings. The NPS lists Chiriaco Summit as a camping option south of the park. Nearby: the Chevron food mart (24 h), Foster's Freeze (8am-9pm) and the coffee shop (6am-11pm). A 2021 reviewer got free water at the station. Some I-10 truck noise. A cyclist camped here in 2016 and sat in the coffee shop until it closed. A Jan 2026 reviewer described a dozen trucks parked in the area, so confirm with the host or the store. It is 68 mi from Blythe and 49 mi from the last water at Wiley's Well.

options.name: Joshua Tree South BLM Dispersed Camping (Cottonwood Springs Rd)
options.priceNote: Free; 14-day limit.
options.locationNote: Cottonwood Springs Rd at I-10 exit 168 (north side), 4 mi west of Chiriaco Summit — 0.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 280 from Casa Grande. Exit 168, then north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd; dirt roads branch east and west just north of the freeway and are passable by car. Camp only in the BLM sections on the NPS map: east of the road between I-10 and the Edison power-line road, west of the road north of the power line, and a block further east. It is checkerboarded with private land, and the NPS says to camp 300+ ft from roadways.
options.booking: None, first come. There are hundreds of fire-ring sites and it effectively never fills.
options.legalityNote: BLM land open to camping (check the posted stay limit)
options.cyclistIntel: 155 Campendium reviews through May 2026; a 2024 tent camper liked it, and the NPS BLM map was updated May 2026. The ground is crushed granite and sand, with little freeway noise. Mostly RVs, busier on weekends; good Verizon/T-Mobile coverage. No water: fill at Chiriaco, 4.3 mi east, or at Cottonwood, 6 mi uphill (needs the $15 park entry). This is also mile ~4 of the Mecca variant.

options.name: Cottonwood Campground (Joshua Tree National Park)
options.priceNote: $35/site/night (up to 6 people and 3 tents), plus a $15 per-person 7-day park entry on a bike. Group tent-only sites cost $55.
options.locationNote: Pinto Basin Rd by the Cottonwood Visitor Center, Joshua Tree National Park — 7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 282 from Casa Grande. Exit 168, then 7 mi north on paved Cottonwood Springs Rd/Pinto Basin Rd, climbing about 1,250 ft (1,750 to 3,000 ft). Slow when loaded; return the same way. The NPS describes the park's paved roads as crumbling and uneven.
options.booking: Reservation only, year-round, on recreation.gov. There is NO cell service at the campground, so book before leaving I-10. Check-in at noon; the campground is open 24 h. Availability on the night of Nov 1: 43-50 sites free for Mon-Thu Nov 2-5 and Mon Nov 9, 26 for Sun Nov 8, but only 1 site (B16) left for each of Fri Nov 6 and Sat Nov 7.
options.cyclistIntel: The only campground with potable water and flush toilets between Blythe and Indio; no showers. Limit is 14 nights Oct-May. A riding group in Dec 2019 found it full, and rangers enforced the rules. The only current park alert is the Geology Tour Rd flood closure, which is not on this route. Worth the climb only for water and a proper site.

bestBet: BLM Mecca Hills – Painted Canyon Rd dispersed camping — tents allowed

options.name: BLM Mecca Hills – Painted Canyon Rd dispersed camping
options.priceNote: Free (BLM limit: 14 days in any 28)
options.locationNote: Painted Canyon Rd off Box Canyon Rd, Mecca, CA 92254 — 4.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 292 from Casa Grande. From Mecca, about 4.5 mi NE on paved Box Canyon Rd (gradual climb), then Painted Canyon Rd: 1–4.5 mi of soft, deep sand wash where cars need 4WD. On a loaded bike that is mostly pushing. BLM: Box Canyon Rd has been CLOSED from Pinto Rd to Painted Canyon Rd since Oct 21, 2026 (flood damage from Post-Tropical Cyclone Rachel), so the pull-offs east of the Painted Canyon Rd junction are cut off.
options.booking: None.
options.legalityNote: Legality not confirmed: read the notes before you pitch
options.cyclistIntel: Camp only along the non-wilderness road corridor: bicycles are banned inside the wilderness. Pit toilets halfway up Painted Canyon Rd (2025). Recreational shooting nearby. The sand wash was probably damaged by the storm. Last resort only.

bestBet: Shadow Hills RV Resort — tents, showers, water

options.name: Shadow Hills RV Resort
options.priceNote: Hipcamp from $39/night plus fees; the lowest rate, probably the tent site. 21 grass tent sites, 10 × 20 ft, no tent supplied.
options.locationNote: 40655 Jefferson St, Indio, CA 92203 — 1.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 311 from Casa Grande. Half a mile off the line in north Indio: Jefferson St at Varner Rd, near I-10.
options.booking: Hipcamp instant book, same day OK (0 hours' notice), or call. Check in on arrival.
options.cyclistIntel: The operator advertises tent sites. Restrooms are a short walk, showers free (2021 review). Pool and spa, laundry, wifi, gated. Can be very windy. Sites by Jefferson St get road noise. Best confirmed tent spot in Indio, at the end of this segment.

options.name: Thousand Trails Palm Springs RV Resort
options.priceNote: No tent site type is offered. Non-member RV sites were about $46/night (Campendium, Dec 2025). WiFi costs extra.
options.locationNote: 77500 Varner Rd, Palm Desert, CA 92211 — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 313 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. On Varner Rd just north of I-10 at Washington St, about 0.5 mi off the line.
options.booking: Non-members can book nightly online. Campsite check-in is at noon; the office is open Mon-Fri 9-5. A reviewer advises arriving in daylight.
options.cyclistIntel: Open for the season 9/15/2026-5/15/2027. Its rules allow '1 RV, 2 vehicles, and 2 tents' per site, but booking only offers RV back-in and pull-through sites. Call and ask whether a tent-only cyclist can take an RV site. It has a pool, spa, showers and laundry, and sits right on the line.

bestBet: DragonflyHill Desert Farm (Hipcamp) — tents, showers, water

options.name: Palm Springs Oasis RV Resort
options.priceNote: No tent rate. Non-member RV site about $95 (Jan 2024 review).
options.locationNote: 36100 Date Palm Dr, Cathedral City, CA 92234 — 0.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 323 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. On Date Palm Dr in Cathedral City, about 0.4 mi off the line.
options.booking: Thousand Trails/Encore booking; ask by phone.
options.cyclistIntel: An Encore/Thousand Trails park. All 140 sites are full-hookup RV pads, mostly long-term guests, under the airport approach. Reviewers complain about the showers. Expect a no on tents, but it is right on the line.

options.name: Happy Traveler RV Park (aka Happy Traveller)
options.priceNote: No tent rate published (call for rates). RV sites about $100 (Nov 2025).
options.locationNote: 211 W Mesquite Ave, Palm Springs, CA 92264 — 1.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 329 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 1.4 mi from the line through south Palm Springs streets to W Mesquite Ave. About 1.1 mi from downtown.
options.booking: Call or email happytrav@hotmail.com. A night manager is on site.
options.cyclistIntel: The only campground in central Palm Springs, sheltered from the valley winds. The operator lists only full-hookup RV sites and says nothing about tents. Call. Reviewers say the bathhouse is dated.

options.name: DragonflyHill Desert Farm (Hipcamp)
options.priceNote: $39/night, $45.93 with Hipcamp fees, for the 'Under Desert Skies' tent/RV site with power and water hookups.
options.locationNote: 21st Ave area between Palm Springs and Desert Hot Springs (exact address after booking) — 9.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 9.6 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Long Canyon Rd/21st Ave (bike router). The last mile is a maintained dirt road. About 200-250 ft of net climbing (to about 770 ft). The host sends directions because phone GPS is often wrong.
options.booking: Request to book (not instant). The host approves, then emails registration and waiver forms, and gives a 15-minute orientation on arrival. Full refund if you cancel 3 or more days ahead. Request at least a day or two before you arrive. · unknown (message the host through Hipcamp)
options.cyclistIntel: The closest good tent spot to Palm Springs: hot outdoor showers, accessible porta-potties, mineral well water and an outdoor kitchen. 575 bookings, 97% recommend. The host warns of frequent high winds and near-freezing winter nights. The pool is winterized mid-Oct to April. It is a sober community farm.

options.name: Palm Springs / Joshua Tree KOA
options.priceNote: Tent rate not found (the KOA site blocks automated reading). A 2021 tent camper called the price 'a bit much'. RV sites ran about $91 (Jun 2025).
options.locationNote: 70405 Dillon Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241 — 11.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 11.7 mi from the line in north Palm Springs (N Palm Canyon at Via Escuela) via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave and Mountain View Rd to Dillon Rd (bike router). The router uses some minor desert roads, and Dillon Rd is the paved fallback. You climb about 500 ft, to roughly 1,040 ft.
options.booking: Book with KOA online or by phone. Office hours and after-hours check-in not confirmed; staff escort guests to sites.
options.cyclistIntel: The only conventional tent campground between Indio and Whitewater: a 287-site resort with a separate tent area (sinks shared), keypad bathhouses with private showers, a hot-spring pool and hot tub, a store and coin laundry. A Mar 2025 review mentions strong wind hitting tents. Reviews run through Mar 2026. The detour is about 23 mi round trip, so treat it as a fallback.

options.name: Joshua Tree, Palm Springs, Coachella Adjacent (private campground, The Dyrt)
options.priceNote: $15-25/night (The Dyrt listing).
options.locationNote: Desert Hot Springs, Dillon Rd/Corkill Rd area (exact address on booking) — 11.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 11.1 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and minor roads near Corkill Rd (bike router). The last roads may be sandy. Climb of about 450 ft.
options.booking: Request to book on The Dyrt (the host approves). Call or text ahead.
options.cyclistIntel: A fenced private desert lot with hot showers, drinking water, toilets and a small camp store, but no shade. The cheapest option in the Desert Hot Springs cluster. Rated 5.0 from 4 reviews dated 2023 to Mar 2026, so it looks active.

options.name: Catalina Spa & RV Resort
options.priceNote: No tent rate. RV sites from $45/night with free electricity and water (operator site, 2026).
options.locationNote: 18800 Corkill Rd, Desert Hot Springs, CA 92241 — 10.4 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 332 from Casa Grande. About 10.4 mi from the line in north Palm Springs via Gene Autry Trail, 20th Ave, Mountain View Rd and Corkill Rd (bike router). Climb of about 400 ft.
options.booking: RV check-in is at noon. After the office closes, resort ambassadors park late arrivals until 9 pm. The manager decides which rigs are accepted.
options.cyclistIntel: Hot-springs RV resort, open year round, under new management. The operator's pages list only RV sites and cottages; The Dyrt has a generic tent/RV tag. Call and ask whether they will take a tent.

options.name: Windy Point x Palm Springs (Hipcamp off-grid lot)
options.priceNote: $30.40/night, $37.63 with Hipcamp fees.
options.locationNote: Palm Oasis Ave area, Windy Point, north Palm Springs (exact address after booking) — 0.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 337 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. Just off CA-111 at Windy Point via Overture Dr/Palm Oasis Ave, about 0.5 mi off the line. You enter over a 6-inch curb.
options.booking: Hipcamp Instant Book. The host sends a custom wind report before your stay. · unknown (message the host through Hipcamp)
options.cyclistIntel: A 7,500 sq ft lot with a 5-ft chain-link fence, a lockable gate, a streetlight and a picnic table. It is completely self-contained: no water, toilet, power or trash, and the host asks you to bring a portable toilet. The host warns that 'Standard free-standing tents generally don't work here' because gusts can reach gale force. Book it only when the forecast is light, and read the host's wind report. NWS shows easterly flow Nov 5-8, which can still gust at the pass mouth. Water and snacks at Windy Cove Market & Gas, 60490 Overture Dr. 98% recommend (20 ratings).

bestBet: Whitewater Preserve campground (Wildlands Conservancy) — tents allowed

options.name: BLM land along lower Whitewater Canyon Rd (Sand to Snow NM), unverified dispersed camping
options.priceNote: Free, if camping is legal there.
options.locationNote: Whitewater Canyon Rd, about 33.958-33.972 N — 5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 341 from Casa Grande. Paved road. About 1.5-2.5 mi up Whitewater Canyon Rd from Bonnie Bell, roughly 5 mi from the line. The BLM parcels are mixed in with private land, and boundaries are not marked as far as we know.
options.booking: None. Unverified; ask BLM before relying on it.
options.legalityNote: Legality not confirmed: read the notes before you pitch
options.cyclistIntel: The BLM land-status map shows BLM parcels beside the lower canyon road inside Sand to Snow National Monument. The monument page sends campers to BLM's general dispersed-camping rules but says nothing about this canyon, and no camper or rider report was found. Last resort only, for example if you miss the preserve's 4:15 pm check-in. Stay out of sight of homes and make no fire. The pass mouth is very windy.

options.name: Whitewater Preserve campground (Wildlands Conservancy)
options.priceNote: Free (donations appreciated).
options.locationNote: 9160 Whitewater Canyon Rd, Whitewater, CA 92282 — 7.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 341 from Casa Grande. Paved. Leave CA-111 at Tipton Rd and follow Whitewater Cutoff to Whitewater Canyon Rd at Bonnie Bell, then 4.2 mi up the 2-lane canyon road to the preserve. That is about 6.5-9.5 mi from the line depending on the turn (the bike router gives 9.5 mi from the I-10/CA-111 junction). You climb about 1,000 ft (roughly 1,100 to 2,190 ft). Next morning, descend and get on I-10 westbound at the Whitewater exit, which is bike-legal there.
options.booking: Reserve at least 48 h ahead with the online request form (check the campground calendar first). Walk-ins are accepted only if the campground is not full and you check in at the ranger station before 4:15 pm. The preserve is open 8 am-5 pm. Check-out 11 am. Up to 3 nights per 30 days; capacity 30 guests a day. Reservations can be cancelled for hazardous weather.
options.cyclistIntel: The best-value stop on the segment: a free tent area with flush toilets, drinking water, a river and ponds. No fires of any kind, no generators, and no cell signal on site (signal starts about 3.5 mi down the road). The WHOLE PRESERVE WAS CLOSED SUN 11/1/2026 for hazardous weather and flood conditions, and the operator warns of more El Nino closures this winter. Confirm with whitewaterpreserve@wildlandsconservancy.org or by phone, and submit the form by about Nov 3 for a Nov 5-6 night. If you miss the 4:15 pm check-in, fall back to the Windy Point lot or to Banning KOA (about 15 mi on, with after-hours self check-in).

options.name: Cabazon Escape (private lot, The Dyrt)
options.priceNote: unknown (the listing shows a $1 placeholder).
options.locationNote: 0.12-acre lot southeast of Cabazon (no street address listed) — 3.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 346 from Casa Grande. Paved local streets. About 3-3.5 mi southeast of central Cabazon via Main St, Broadway, Bonita Ave and Almond St (the bike router gives 5.5 mi from the I-10 line). At about 1,520 ft, it is lower than Cabazon.
options.booking: Request to book on The Dyrt, or by phone or email.
options.cyclistIntel: Listed in 2023 for tents and RVs. One of its two reviews (2023) called it 'more like a landfill' and left at once; the other, by a Dyrt staffer, praised waterfall access. It may be inactive. Call first; it is the only private listing at the Cabazon end.

bestBet: Banning Stagecoach KOA — tents, showers, water

options.name: Silent Valley Club (membership RV resort)
options.priceNote: unknown (membership resort).
options.locationNote: Poppet Flats Rd off CA-243, south of Banning — 10.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 353 from Casa Grande. Paved but a big climb. About 9 mi south up CA-243 (San Gorgonio Ave) from Banning, then about 1 mi west on Poppet Flats Rd (10.6 mi by bike router). Net climb about 1,250 ft, to roughly 3,580 ft. Not practical on a loaded bike.
options.booking: Membership basis; whether non-members can stay is not stated. · unknown
options.cyclistIntel: Listed with tent sites, but it is members-only and far uphill. Included only so it is not mistaken for a nearby option.

options.name: Banning Stagecoach KOA
options.priceNote: Tent rate not found (koa.com blocks automated reading). Recent nightly reports, probably for RV sites: $50 (2022) and $54 (2025). Tent sites 95-99 have water only, no power.
options.locationNote: 1455 S San Gorgonio Ave, Banning, CA 92220 — 1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 354 from Casa Grande. Paved and slightly downhill. From Ramsey St (the line) ride about 1 mi south on S San Gorgonio Ave (CA-243) under I-10. The ride back up next morning is mild, about 120 ft.
options.booking: Book with KOA online or by phone. The office closes around 5-6 pm (2022 review), but self check-in is available after hours; registration packets are left at the office.
options.cyclistIntel: The only campground in the Cabazon-Banning-Beaumont stretch confirmed to take tents (sites 95-99), and the safest late-arrival option in the pass. It is gravel and RV-oriented (a 2016 reviewer said it is 'really not for tent camping'), with one bathhouse. 2025-26 reviews report broken sprinklers, overgrown grass and occasional broken toilets. The pool is closed in winter, and train horns carry at night. Reviews continue through May 2026.

bestBet: Bogart Regional Park campground (Cherry Valley) — tents allowed

options.name: Country Hills RV Park
options.priceNote: No tent rate. Full-hookup RV site $68/night for 2 people, plus a one-time $15 resort fee (operator site, 2026). Showers take quarters.
options.locationNote: 14711 Manzanita Park Rd, Beaumont, CA 92223 — 1.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 359 from Casa Grande. Paved. About 1.7 mi from the line in Beaumont via Pennsylvania Ave, 1st St, Michigan Ave and Roadrunner Dr, south of I-10 (bike router). The park is gated and needs a gate card.
options.booking: Book online or by phone with a credit card; cancel at least 72 h ahead. Check-in 1 pm. Gated, so call ahead for a late arrival (a 2023 guest arranged one).
options.cyclistIntel: The park rules are written entirely for RVs and say nothing about tents; The Dyrt's 'tent sites' tag is generic. Call before counting on it. Laundry is reported to cost $10 a load because of a card system.

options.name: Noble Creek Regional Park RV campground (Beaumont-Cherry Valley Recreation and Park District)
options.priceNote: $35/night (2022) to $35-50 (The Dyrt), for RV sites. There are 9 dry sites.
options.locationNote: 650 W Oak Valley Pkwy, Beaumont, CA 92223 — 0.8 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 361 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat. About 0.8 mi west of Beaumont Ave on Oak Valley Pkwy.
options.booking: Required. Currently by phone or office@bcvparks.com to the district office only (Mon-Thu 8-5, Fri 8-noon). No on-site check-in was reported.
options.cyclistIntel: The district's 2026 brochure lists 24 full-hookup, 15 half-hookup and 9 dry-camping sites. 2022 reviewers called it a parking lot with no visitor restrooms. The Dyrt shows tent sites and toilets, but no review confirms tents. A district notice says the park was closed for fire-camp operations one summer. Call.

options.name: Bogart Regional Park campground (Cherry Valley)
options.priceNote: $35/night (sites 1-30); pets $2/day (district fee page).
options.locationNote: 9600 International Park Rd (Cherry Ave), Cherry Valley, CA 92223 — 2.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 362 from Casa Grande. Paved, with about 400 ft of climbing (2,785 to 3,180 ft). From the line at Beaumont Ave and Cherry Valley Blvd, ride 2.3 mi via Cherry Valley Blvd, Live Oak Ave, Vineland/Noble/Dutton St and Cherry Ave (bike router). It is about 2 mi past the segment end.
options.booking: Book by phone or office@bcvparks.com with the district office, Mon-Thu 8-5 and Fri 8-noon. Online booking is suspended 'until further notice'. The park is open 7 am-sundown, with an attendant only Sat-Sun 8-3. The gate may be shut in the evening (a reviewer arriving after 5 pm worked the gate switch themselves). Max stay 7 nights.
options.cyclistIntel: A shaded foothill campground run by the local park district with flush restrooms and drinking water. At 3,180 ft it runs a few degrees colder than Banning, where lows of 51-57 F are forecast. The district warns of bears, and a campfire ban was in place at its last notice. Tents were barred during COVID (a cyclist found it closed to tents in 2021), but reviewers tent-camped in Aug 2025. Call by Friday noon for a weekend night.

options.name: Fisherman's Retreat (San Timoteo Canyon)
options.priceNote: unknown
options.locationNote: 32300 San Timoteo Canyon Rd, Redlands, CA 92373 — 6.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 368 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 6.3 mi from Cherry Valley Blvd/Calimesa Blvd (mile ~358.6) via Palmer Ave and San Timoteo Canyon Rd, about 785 ft downhill going in. On to Redlands is 10–11 mi via San Timoteo Canyon Rd and Alessandro Rd (470–730 ft of climbing), rejoining the line at ~mile 366–368, so the detour costs about 10 mi.
options.booking: Unknown; call. It is a membership resort (Halo Resorts) with a separate non-member area.
options.cyclistIntel: Private RV resort on three stocked fishing lakes, with a store, restaurant and pool. Runs as a membership park with a non-member section. The Dyrt lists showers, drinking water and toilets. Non-member nightly rates, tent policy and 2026 status are all unverified (no website, Facebook only). Long detour into the canyon.

bestBet: Yucaipa Regional Park — tents, showers, water

options.name: Yucaipa Regional Park
options.priceNote: Tent spaces A–I. The county lists $35 Mon–Thu / $45 Fri–Sun for no-hookup sites (max 6 people), and group tent camping at $5/person plus a $20 group fee. Add a $10 non-refundable reservation fee. Seniors/veterans/military get $5 off Sun–Thu. Expect roughly $35–55 total for one person.
options.locationNote: 33900 Oak Glen Rd, Yucaipa, CA 92399 — 4.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 370 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 4.7 mi from Calimesa Blvd (Hist US 99, mile ~360.8) via Avenue G, Wildwood Canyon Rd, Yucaipa Blvd and 5th St to Oak Glen Rd, about 570 ft of climbing. On to Redlands via Oak Glen Rd, Avenue D, 17th St and Tennessee St is about 7 mi, rejoining at ~mile 366, so the detour costs about 6 mi. Stay on paved roads; routers may suggest the Crafton Hills Ridge Trail.
options.booking: Online only at parkreservations.sbcounty.gov, at least 24 h ahead (no same-day booking). Check-in 3 pm. If you arrive after the 5 pm closing, go straight to your site; after-hours instructions come in the confirmation email (check spam). Park hours are 7:30 am–5 pm from Oct 31, 2026 to May 2027.
options.cyclistIntel: San Bernardino County park with 9 designated tent spaces (A–I on the park map) next to the 42-site RV loop; tents are allowed only there. The county lists hot showers and restrooms, but a 2024 reviewer in group site A said there were no showers near the tent area. Potable water, fire rings, three fishing lakes. A June 2025 reviewer camped in 'tent site E'. Elevation about 2,600 ft, and power-safety shutoffs are possible. The park also closes on the third Wednesday of November (Nov 18), after his window.

options.name: The Unhitched Ranch (Hipcamp)
options.priceNote: $99.51/night base for the ranch's RV/tent site (about $117 with Hipcamp fees)
options.locationNote: Reche Canyon, Colton/Loma Linda area (exact address after booking) — 9.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 381 from Casa Grande. Paved but hilly: about 9 mi from Barton Rd (Loma Linda, mile ~372.7) via Barton Rd and Reche Canyon Rd, a narrow two-lane canyon road with commuter traffic; about 900 ft of climbing. Leave via Reche Canyon Rd and Washington St to Colton (7.5 mi, rejoining at ~mile 375), so the detour costs about 14 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
options.booking: Hipcamp request-to-book (the host approves). Usually one group at a time on the ranch. · unknown (message the host through Hipcamp)
options.cyclistIntel: Family-run Clydesdale and longhorn ranch of about 40 acres, with wild burros nearby. Potable water, toilets, laundry, Wi-Fi, electric and water hookups, campfires allowed. 168 bookings, 100% recommend. Expensive for one rider, and the climb in is steep. The Hipcamp map pin is approximate.

options.name: Riverview Ranch (Hipcamp)
options.priceNote: $33.25/night base for the tent site (about $39 with Hipcamp fees)
options.locationNote: Jurupa Valley near Mt. Rubidoux (exact address after booking) — 8.7 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 390 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 8.7 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Riverview Dr, mostly downhill (about 550 ft). Back to the Pacific Electric Trail is about 11 mi via Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave (about 650 ft up, rejoining at ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 16 mi.
options.booking: Hipcamp instant book; arrival details come after booking. · unknown (message the host through Hipcamp)
options.cyclistIntel: Private, shaded property near Mt. Rubidoux and the Santa Ana River. The listing promises clean bathrooms and hot showers, plus potable water, a shared fire ring, picnic tables and Wi-Fi. The tent site has 36 bookings and the listing is 95% recommended. It is next door to Rancho Jurupa and is a cheaper, quieter alternative. The map pin is approximate.

options.name: Rancho Jurupa Regional Park
options.priceNote: $40–55 per site per night (2025–26 reports; $55 is full hookup). No separate tent rate found.
options.locationNote: 4800 Crestmore Rd, Jurupa Valley (Riverside), CA 92509 — 8.9 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 390 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 8.9 mi south from the line in Rialto (mile ~383) via Cactus Ave, Bloomington Ave, Cedar Ave, 34th St and Wallace St, mostly downhill (about 500 ft). To rejoin, take Crestmore Rd, Rubidoux Blvd and Locust Ave to the Pacific Electric Trail (11 mi, about 650 ft up, ~mile 386), so the detour costs about 17 mi.
options.booking: Reserve at rivcoparks.org or 800-234-7275. Walk-ups register at the staffed entrance gate (single-file line). Late arrivals with a reservation get gate, bathroom and laundry codes (Dec 2025 review).
options.cyclistIntel: Large Riverside County campground on the Santa Ana River. The Lakeview side has gravel roads with water/electric sites; the Cottonwood side has paved full-hookup sites. Tents are allowed. Showers on both sides (tokens on the Lakeview side), laundry, a small store, ranger patrols. Busy and loud on weekends. A ranger warned campers to lock up bikes in 2020. rivcoparks.org blocks automated fetches, so fees come from reviews.

bestBet: Harmony Heaven Campyard (Hipcamp) — tents, showers, water

options.name: Harmony Heaven Campyard (Hipcamp)
options.priceNote: $64/night base for 'Starlight', a pre-pitched 4-person safari tent (about $75 with fees). A-frame campers from $79.
options.locationNote: Alta Loma, Rancho Cucamonga (exact address after booking) — 3.5 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 406 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 3.5 mi north of the Pacific Electric Trail (mile ~397.6) via Hellman Ave, Lemon Ave, Beryl St and Carnelian St, about 570 ft of climbing. Back down to the trail at Carnelian St is 4 mi (~mile 399), so the detour costs about 6 mi. The exact address comes after booking.
options.booking: Hipcamp instant book. · unknown (message the host through Hipcamp)
options.cyclistIntel: Private half-acre 'campyard'. You sleep in the host's safari tent; no bring-your-own-tent site is listed, so ask the host. Private outdoor bathroom with a hot shower, outdoor kitchen, fire pit, pool, Wi-Fi, laundry and farm animals. 12 bookings, 100% recommend. It is the only tent-style stay near the Pacific Electric Trail between Rialto and Pomona. The map pin is approximate.

options.name: Marshall Canyon Regional Park campground
options.priceNote: unknown
options.locationNote: La Verne foothills, CA 91750 (street address not verified) — 6.3 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 415 from Casa Grande. Paved and steep: about 6.3 mi north from Bonita Ave/White Ave in La Verne (mile ~407) into the foothills, about 1,070 ft of climbing.
options.booking: Reservation only, through LA County Parks (reservations.lacounty.gov). It appears geared to groups. LA County regional parks are closed Mondays and Tuesdays. · unknown
options.cyclistIntel: LA County says the park has 'forty campsites' with barbecues and a fire circle, available for reservation, next to the Marshall Canyon equestrian center. I found no details on individual bookings, fees or restrooms. Long climb. Use it only if Bonelli Bluffs and Fairplex are full.

options.name: Fairplex RV Park (former Los Angeles/Pomona Fairplex KOA)
options.priceNote: unknown; call (2020 reports: about $50–75 per site)
options.locationNote: 2200 N White Ave, Pomona, CA 91768 — 1.1 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 416 from Casa Grande. Paved and flat: 1.1 mi from Bonita Ave via White Ave (mile ~408). Back to Bonita Ave is 2.1 mi, so the detour costs about 2 mi.
options.booking: Call or book online; 72-h cancellation policy. Office hours are not published.
options.cyclistIntel: 183 full-hookup sites plus cabins beside the LA County Fairgrounds. Showers, laundry, heated pool and spa, mini-market, free Wi-Fi. As a KOA it sold tent sites with electric (2020 review), and The Dyrt and Campendium still list tent sites. It is no longer a KOA, and its own website now advertises only RV sites and cabins, so confirm tents by phone. Sites are tight and some are near traffic. The new Metro A Line stations at La Verne and Pomona (opened Sept 2025) are within a couple of miles.

options.name: Bonelli Bluffs RV Resort & Campground
options.priceNote: $30/night walk-in tent site for up to 2 people; +$10 per extra person (max 6); pets $2/day
options.locationNote: 1440 Camper View Rd, San Dimas, CA 91773 — 2.6 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 418 from Casa Grande. Paved: about 2.6 mi from Bonita Ave (San Dimas, mile ~409) via Wheeler Ave and Puddingstone Dr to the resort entrance on Camper View Rd, about 200 ft of climbing onto the bluff. Continue via Puddingstone Dr and Walnut Ave back to Bonita Ave (3.7 mi, ~mile 411), so the detour costs about 4 mi. Avoid the park's dirt trails that routers suggest.
options.booking: Tent sites can't be booked online; call 909-599-8355. The guest-service lobby and market are open Sun–Wed 8 am–5 pm and Thu–Sat 8 am–7 pm. A kiosk is open 24 h, with an after-hours line.
options.cyclistIntel: The best-equipped tent option in the LA basin: walk-in grass tent sites with picnic tables and fire pits above Puddingstone Lake. Clean restrooms, showers, laundry (6 am–11 pm), two pools, a market and free Wi-Fi. The tent area is on a slope with a carry from parking, so wheel the bike in. Expect small-plane noise from Brackett Field and occasional late weekend parties. LA County day-use areas close Mon/Tue, but the resort office lists hours every day. It is 31 line-miles from the theater, and the Metro A Line San Dimas station is a few miles away.

bestBet: Gould Mesa Trail Camp (Angeles NF) — tents allowed

options.name: Gould Mesa Trail Camp (Angeles NF)
options.priceNote: Free (no camping fee; the Adventure Pass applies only to parked vehicles)
options.locationNote: Gabrielino Trail, Arroyo Seco, about 2 mi above the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead, Altadena/La Cañada Flintridge — 6.2 mi off the I-10 line at corridor mile 443 from Casa Grande. 6.2 mi from Colorado Blvd (Pasadena, mile ~434.6): Orange Grove Blvd, Rosemont Ave and Arroyo Blvd to the Windsor Ave/Ventura St trailhead (paved, about 600 ft up), then 2 mi up the Gabrielino Trail (dirt and broken pavement, several creek crossings; bikes allowed). About 820 ft of climbing in all. From camp to the Elysian Theater is 11.9 mi.
options.booking: First-come, first-served; no reservations. Arrive before dark because of the creek crossings (sunset about 4:55 pm).
options.cyclistIntel: Free primitive trail camp with about 6–10 sites, tables, fire rings, a vault toilet and bear boxes. No potable water (creek only, treat it) and no showers. Steady day-hiker and mountain-bike traffic. It is not in the Eaton Fire closure, which shut the Millard and Idlehour camps through 2027, and a Feb 2026 reviewer used it. The new USFS website has no page for it, though, so call the district to confirm. Fire danger is 'Very High': no wood fires. It is the closest legal tent site to the Elysian Theater. Stay limit is 14 days.
